rollback_evidence: ios etherchannel (IOS-M027), measured on IOSvL2 15.2(20200924:215240) (switch) in the virtual topology Cisco IOSvL2 15.2. Same table and lines as the IOS XE profile (xe etherchannel): key = a physical Ethernet port; create = the port joins a channel-group, update = another LACP mode or another group, delete = the port leaves its group. Lines: 'interface PORT', 'channel-group N mode active|passive' ('channel-group ?' answers <1-255>, 'interface port-channel ?' answers <1-48>; a missing port-channel is created by IOS, 'Creating a port-channel interface Port-channel N', and the running configuration gets an empty 'interface Port-channelN' block; N above the platform limit is refused with 'Command rejected (Port-channel49, Gi1/1): Invalid group(slot) number' and changes nothing, which the safeguard return handles like any refused line); the same group with another mode is changed in place. Unlike IOS XE, IOSvL2 moves a member to another group directly and creates the new port-channel, but Admin keeps the unbundling line 'no channel-group' (no number) before the new group so that one plan serves both platforms. The member port keeps its own switchport lines (IOSvL2 does not copy the port-channel configuration); a mismatch of mode or access VLAN only suspends the port ('Probable reason: access vlan of Gi1/3 is 10, Po43 is 20'), so Admin aligns the access VLAN of the port with a configured access port-channel before the join. 'no channel-group' leaves the port-channel interface in place and, unlike removing a port-channel with members, does not shut the port down; 'no interface Port-channelN' of a port-channel that still has members removes their membership AND adds 'shutdown' to each of them, so Admin sends it only for a port-channel without members. 'no channel-group' on a non-member and an absent 'no interface Port-channelN' ('% Invalid input detected') are harmless. PAgP and static modes (on, auto, desirable) and channel-protocol lines are outside the profile. The safeguard is the revert timer of the interface profile. Refused before any write: a port that is not an explicit access port (trunk, dynamic auto/desirable), a routed port, a port with an address, a routed or management port-channel, the management interface or VLAN, a port with an LLDP/CDP neighbor, learned MAC addresses, an up link or a port in a bundle. The check account (privilege 1) reads show interfaces PORT etherchannel ('Etherchannel not enabled on this port' outside any group; 'Port state = Up Mstr Not-in-Bndl' of a member without a partner, 'Up Cnt-bndl-rmt Suspend Mstr Rmt-LACP_Dsbl Not-in-Bndl' of a second one).
